# Statistical Tests: Comparison of Medians or Means

## Make Clear What Is a Statistical Test, and When to Use It

Reference: `(Vu & Harrington, 2020)`

### Mean and Median

| Concept | Definition & Reference |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **Mean** | The sum of all values divided by the total number of values. Ch. 1, 1.4.1 *Measures of center: mean and median*, p. **30** |
| **Median** | The middle value when the observations are ordered from smallest to largest. Ch. 1, 1.4.1 *Measures of center: mean and median*, p. **30** |

### Variance and Standard Deviation

| Concept | Definition & Reference |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **Variance** | A measure of how spread out the values are around the mean. A large variance means the values are more spread out. Ch. 1, 1.4.2 *Measures of spread*, p. **31** |
| **Standard deviation** | Square root of the variance. Another measure of spread. How far values tend to be from the mean, in the same units as the data. Ch. 1, 1.4.2 *Measures of spread*, p. **31** |

### Normal Distribution

| Concept | Definition & Reference |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **Normal distribution** | A symmetric, bell-shaped distribution where most values are close to the mean. A perfectly normal distribution, the mean, median, and mode are equal. Ch. 3, 3.3 *Normal distribution*, pp. **152–153** |

### Statistical Test

| Concept | Definition & Reference |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **Statistical test** | A method used to decide whether a difference or relationship in the sample is likely to be real or could just be due to random chance. usually starting with a null hypothesis (\$H_0\$). used when we want to determine whether an observed difference/association in a sample provides sufficient evidence of a corresponding effect in the population, while accounting for sampling variability. Ch. 4, 4.3 *Hypothesis testing*, p. **212-214** |

### When to Use a Statistical Test

| Concept | Definition & Reference |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **When to Use a Statistical Test** | used when we want to determine whether an observed difference/association in a sample provides sufficient evidence of a corresponding effect in the population, while accounting for sampling variability. Ch. 4, 4.3 *Hypothesis testing*, p. **212-214** |

### Parametric and Non-Parametric Tests

| Concept | Definition & Reference |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **Parametric test** | A statistical test used for normally distributed data and makes more assumptions about the data. Ch. 4, 4.3 *Hypothesis testing*, p. **212-214**. Ch. 5, pp. **238, 245, 248** |
| **Non-parametric test** | A statistical test used for non-normally distributed data and makes fewer assumptions. Ch. 4, 4.3 *Hypothesis testing*, p. **212-214**. Ch. 5, pp. **238, 245, 248** |

### Assumptions of Parametric Tests

| Concept | Definition & Reference |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **Assumptions of Parametric Tests** | Assumptions: normally distributed data, independent observations, and for some group comparisons, similar variances between groups. Ch. 4, 4.3 *Hypothesis testing*, p. **212-214**. Ch. 5, pp. **238, 245, 248** |

### Assumptions of Non-Parametric Tests

| Concept | Definition & Reference |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **Assumptions of Non-Parametric Tests** | Assumptions: Not normally distributed data, appropriately measured data, independence of observations when comparing independent groups. Ch. 4, 4.3 *Hypothesis testing*, p. **212-214**. Ch. 5, pp. **238, 245, 248** |

### p-value

| Concept | Definition & Reference |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **p-value** | Tells us how unusual our result would be if there were actually no real effect or difference. A small p-value means the result would be unlikely under the null hypothesis. Ch. 4, 4.3.1, Step 4, p. **214** |

### Risk of Error When Using a Statistical Test

| Concept | Definition & Reference |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **Risk of Error When Using a Statistical Test** | When performing a statistical test, we evaluate a sample to draw conclusions about a population. Because we rely on probabilities, there is always a risk of making an incorrect decision regarding the null hypothesis. **(**Ch. 4, 4.3.4 *Decision errors*, pp. **220–221)** |

### Paired and Unpaired Tests

| Concept | Definition & Reference |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **Paired test** | Used when observations are related, such as measurements taken from the same participants before and after treatment. Ch. 5, 5.2 *Two-sample test for paired data*, pp. **244–246** |
| **Unpaired test** | Used when the groups are independent, containing different observations or participants. Ch. 5, 5.3 *Two-sample test for independent data*, pp. **247–250** |
